summary: Streaming response stalls mid-generation without connection close or error
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports chat streaming connections (SSE and WebSocket proxy path) that appear to stall mid-generation: the connection remains open and the server sends no FIN/RST, no 5xx, and no explicit error, but the client sees no further token chunks for 15–60s and eventually times out.

Impact:
- Affects a subset of long-turn chat requests (>512 tokens) for FastDocs (dedicated tenant).
- Causes degraded UX: partial answers and client-side timeouts, occasional double-requests from the UI.

Environment:
- Tenant: FastDocs, Inc. (dedicated)
- Region: prod.us-east (us-east-1)
- API path: POST /v1/chat/stream (SSE) behind streaming-proxy v2.1.4 and api-gateway v3.2.
- Observed on models: redwood-realtime-7b (primary), occasional on llama-2-13b-chat fallback.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Start a long-chat session with prompt that generates multi-paragraph answers (context ~800 tokens).
2) Use the web-app with SSE client that expects periodic comment heartbeats.
3) Observe that after ~30–90s of initial token flow, the stream emits nothing for >20s; the client marks as idle and either shows spinner indefinitely or triggers a retry.

What we observed (support capture):
- We reproduced with customer's prompt and toggled stream parameters. On several runs, the server-side application logs show active request and the runtime still holding KV cache, but no outgoing chunks are emitted for a window of time. No 5xx entries in api-gateway logs.
- tcpdump from a customer sim-proxy session shows TCP connection alive with keepalives; no TLS renegotiation.
- streaming-proxy logs show the request routed to a serving node and that node produced token batches, but proxy did not forward last few batches until a subsequent token batch arrived (i.e., proxy aggregated chunks and delayed flush).

Expected behavior:
- Server should stream token chunks as they are generated (or emit heartbeat comments) so client sees progress. Long gaps without emitted events should not occur.

Temporary workaround suggested to customer:
- Enable client-side longer idle threshold (increase client timeout from 15s to 120s).
- For immediate mitigation, pin to a model variant with faster decoder latency (redwood-realtime-7b-fast) while we investigate proxy flushing behavior.

Attachments:
- Customer-provided tcpdump excerpt and browser console logs.
- Internal proxy and runtime sampling traces (linked in investigation notes).
comments: 2026-02-20 09:12 - Aisha Patel (Support): Ticket opened with customer logs and reproduction. Assigned to on-call infra eng.

2026-02-20 10:03 - Liam O'Connor (Infra): Reproduced locally with customer's prompt. Noted that serving node returns token batches but proxy flush interval spikes. Captured proxy trace: https://logs.redwood.internal/trace/stream/75333

2026-02-20 14:27 - Elena Ruiz (SRE): Observed increased buffering in streaming-proxy v2.1.4 when backend response latency oscillates between 20–200ms per token. Hypothesis: adaptive aggregator is coalescing small chunks and waiting for a threshold before flush, which interacts poorly with SSE consumers expecting progressive output.

2026-02-21 08:45 - Liam O'Connor (Infra): Rolled a canary of proxy with aggressive flush (config flush_threshold=1, max_delay_ms=200) to staging. Early signs: reduced idle gaps. Planning controlled prod canary for 2026-02-22.

2026-02-23 11:02 - Customer (FastDocs): Confirmed that increasing client timeout is an acceptable temporary fix but requests permanent resolution because users experience double-posting when UI retries.
investigation_notes: 2026-02-20 - Captured end-to-end traces correlating serving-runtime token emission timestamps with proxy forward timestamps. In many cases token generation is continuous but proxy forward is bursty.

2026-02-20 - Proxy code path: adaptive_coalescer waits until either buffer_size >= threshold OR time_since_first_chunk >= coalesce_window. coalesce_window defaults to 1s but internal backpressure metrics pushed coalesce_window to 5s under transient throughput drops.

2026-02-21 - Hypothesis A: coalescer backpressure policy is too aggressive when per-token latency variability is high (long-tail), causing visible client stalls even though backend is making progress.

2026-02-21 - Hypothesis B: SSE clients expect comment-style heartbeats when token production pauses; runtime currently does not emit keepalive comments during token gaps shorter than 10s. Combining the two leads to long perceived stalls.
2026-02-22 - Reproduced proxy behavior in staging using fault-injection to simulate token-latency jitter. Adjusting max_delay_ms to 200ms eliminated the stall in 95% of runs.
resolution_notes: Planned fix: update streaming-proxy (v2.1.5) to set default coalesce_window max to 250ms and add explicit SSE keepalive passthrough for comment lines (':keepalive') emitted by serving-runtime. Deployed canary 2026-02-22 to 3% of traffic in prod.us-east; monitoring for regressions. Work items: (1) runtime: enable periodic keepalive comments when token gaps >150ms (PR #834), (2) proxy: tighten coalescer bounds and expose config for tenants with long-chat patterns. Post-deploy customer validation with FastDocs scheduled 2026-02-24. If canary is green for 48h we will roll to 100% and close ticket.
